scope: Isolated S1 content-process exit and kill before document construction, and recovery from an error page through reload, back, forward, and a new URL. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.

baseline.head: 1b916d0
baseline.note: The construction evidence records three passing runs in each mode at dde097c. 1b916d0 changed only documentation.

owner_requirement: An error page is recoverable by navigating back, reloading, or editing the target URL and trying again (recorded 2026-11-24 in docs/phase-3-plan.md).

configuration.pending_process_probe: The existing exit and kill barrier now accepts the content process of a view's newest pending top-level pipeline. The host withholds that pipeline's navigation response, so it has no document.
configuration.history_fixture: The pending-navigation view loads a first page and then the source page before its pending navigation fails. After recovery the fixture reloads, goes back, goes forward, and loads a new URL.

defects.name: Pending pipeline treated as ordinary teardown
defects.observed: The lifeline handler counted a pipeline as live only if its browsing context held it. A pending pipeline joins its browsing context only at activation. When the only child of a new view died, the host received the pipeline-exit Active(None) but no crash notification. When the child of a live view's pending navigation died, the view sent no notification, kept a stale pending change, and could no longer navigate: a load of a new URL did not complete within 8 seconds.
defects.fix: A pipeline is also live while its view holds it as a pending change. Lifeline loss then enters the existing panic handler.
defects.diagnostic_note: Diagnostic run before the fix, in both exit and kill modes. Its fixture variant is not retained.

defects.name: Crash recovery left history entries on closed pipelines
defects.observed: Upstream crash recovery closes every pipeline in the top browsing context, including inactive history entries, without marking those entries for reload. Its crash-document change replaces NeedsToReload::Yes(active), which never matches the stored NeedsToReload::No(active). Back after recovery activated a closed pipeline. The view then had no active document, and every later evaluation and load failed with InternalError. Forward failed the same way on the replaced entry.
defects.fix: Before recovery, the panic handler converts every pipeline of the top browsing context to NeedsToReload::Yes with its refreshed load data, as history eviction and document discard already do.
defects.scope_note: This applies to every crash path that reaches the panic handler, not only pending navigation failure. Nested browsing-context history entries remain unchecked.

findings: Reload, back, forward, and a new URL all recover from the error page in both modes. Each restored document receives a fresh identity, and the engine rejects the departed scopes.

Servo sends the crash load through embedder request interception after it sets the crash network error, and an intercepted response replaces that error. The fixture intercepts every page, so every recovery document in this probe is the source page served by the fixture, not Servo's error page. The product does not intercept top-level loads today. P3.5 request hooks and P3.7 bulwark:// delivery must not override crash loads.
Because of that interception, reload in this fixture reloads the source page. Reload of a real Servo error page remains unverified.

Remaining replacement audits remain open.

local_validation.patch_reproduction: The patch applies to the published packages with patch -F 0 and no offsets. A fresh preparation reproduces the development sources byte for byte.
local_validation.binary_isolation: Each run used a private copy of its binary. The final build was rebuilt after the negative controls and matches the SHA-256 of both passing final reports.
local_validation.product_changes: None. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, product crates, and installed natives are unchanged.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
Exit and kill happen at a barrier in the pending child. Failures during parsing, after headers, and in about:blank or srcdoc construction remain untested.
History recovery is checked for top-level entries after one failure path. Nested browsing-context history and other crash paths rely on the same handler but have no dedicated fixture.
Fixture interception replaces every crash document, so no case observes Servo's real error page.
The host allocation counter is not a production registry or handle revocation mechanism.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
